en: Victorious is the Supreme Lord, whose majesty of bliss is made to overflow by the sight of her who gazes with sweet speech that captivates the heart.
Victorious is he, the unconquered one, who is flourishing with the wealth of glory, compassion, awakening, and supreme bliss, and whose majesty is illuminated by wisdom.
Homage to Śaṅkara, who is like an ocean of milk, whose nature consists of pure nectar, in whom the *bindu* and *nāda* expand, and who is infinite light.
We hate you; we praise you; we address our prayers to you, O Lord of Ambikā!
Out of your great affection, you have rightly sustained us in every way.

Homage to Śambhu, the all-pervading Lord, whose nature is the illusory power of space, who has withdrawn the contact with sensory objects, and who brings forth the fullness of the nectar of immortality.
We bow to that supreme form of the Lord, which is the universal commonality— undivided even when things are divided, and indeed uncut even when things are cut asunder.
Salutations to Sthāṇu, who is subtler than even the half-measure above the Praṇava, who is greater than the great,
and whose qualities consist of the absence of qualities (nirguṇya) even beyond the cosmic egg.
We praise the power of the Supreme Lord, who is like a swan— pervading the sky and moving everywhere— possessing the female swan as his consort, who contains within her womb the entire universe.

Homage to that wielder of the trident, who is praiseworthy for his artistic skill, who creates the variegated spectacle of the world without any material substrate and even without a wall [upon which to paint].
Having properly extracted and purified the milk of Śiva-knowledge from the belly of the water of illusion, come, O Haṃsa of Hara, and give it to us! BhStc_10 //
Although you possess the distinctions of the six means of valid cognition and their various divisions, you are non-dual;
we offer this oblation to you, Bhava, who are the single ultimate reality.
O Lord, may we behold your inner cave, profound and beautiful, with its darkness wiped away by a supreme light on all sides.
Homage also to those who, even in their dreams, behold the Lord who bestows supreme bliss and whose crest is adorned with a digit of the moon.
O Blessed One, to whom would your disposition—not inclined toward worldly existence, yet skilled in cutting through the fear of rebirth—not be pleasing? BhStc_14 //
O Lord of the World, may this be our duty for as long as we live:
that state which, through your grace, consists of a mind focused solely on you. (BhStc 15)
Homage to Śambhu, whose self consists of the Vedas and Āgamas spread across a thousand branches, and who is a wish-fulfilling tree that produces infinite fruits.
O Lord, having applied the actions of speech, mind, and body unto You,
and having become one with You, might we perhaps at some time be free from the pairs of opposites?
Salutations to the wielder of the trident, who possesses a power independent of anything else in the creation, destruction, and the various beneficial arrangements of the worlds.
For those who meditate even upon the name of Dhūrjaṭi— the primary object of meditation who has transcended all qualities— what further fruit could there be from meditations based on other supports?
Those who, relying on the power of the mantra "Namo namaḥ śivāya," are intent upon enjoying the auspicious prosperity of Śambhu, are truly praiseworthy.

O Lord, what path is there by which You cannot be reached? What speech is there by which You are not expressed? What meditation is there by which You are not to be meditated upon? Or what is there that You are not? (BhStc 21)
"‘This one has been honored, this one has been meditated upon, this one has been satisfied’—may such a sentiment increase within you toward me through a thousand streams. (BhStc 22)
The recollection of you is the sole medicine for the cataract of ignorance;
O Bhava, please show me your favor by granting it to me.
Salutation to Īśa, the accomplisher of all human goals without exception;
for even a prostration made to him by the wise in this world is itself worthy of being saluted.
In this vast and terrible ocean of existence, the abode of the sea-monsters of suffering,
what has not been conquered after obtaining the wish-fulfilling gem of devotion to Śiva?
O Dhūrjaṭi, you are said to be known only by those rare few who possess the wealth of unwavering knowledge that is free from obscuration and beyond all duality; for they alone truly know you.

Though devoid of qualities, the unborn One, who is free from desire yet is the supreme fruit of all desires by his very nature, is victorious as the sole object of knowledge for those who know the qualities.
O Lord, that sovereignty of yours is innate; it is for the sake of obtaining the nectar of the jewel of glory that even the gods do not suffer there in the Ocean of Milk.
Obeisance with devotion to you, Bhava, who protects those who have fallen;
to Śambhu, who bestows auspiciousness through remembrance and praise upon beings in this world and beyond.
O Lord, for those endowed with the knowledge that "You are all-knowing, all-doing,
and everything," what object of knowledge or action is not offered by You for the sake of infinity?
O Protector, if even such a fruit as these three worlds proceeds from mere desire,
who can know the extent of the ultimate reach of your deeds?
I bow to him by whose series of steps of karma even Brahmā and the other gods run higher and higher to attain his abode.
May that Bhava protect you— he by whom this creeper of power has blossomed, thinking, "This is Brahmā, this is Mahendra, and these two are the sun and the moon."
We praise Mṛḍa, whose end cannot be found even by those with deluded internal organs,
and whose limit remains inaccessible even to those who have gone far away.
Homage to the beloved Kapardin, who possesses a multitude of blisses, [to be found] in praise, remembrance, meditation, vision, touch, and likewise in attainment.
O Supreme Lord, even though you have thought, "What is the use of pride?
in your mind, why do you not rejoice in yourself with joy, thinking, "I am one with You through pride"?
Even after contemplating millions of things to be done, due to the fickleness of the mind, one tires;
therefore, O Bhava, may I rest intensely in the bliss of your own mind.
O Lord, if even this triple world is but a mere fraction of you when you are subtle,
then why is it not clearly visible when you are gross, even to Brahmā and the other gods?
If it were not the case that you alone are the one to be addressed by them, O Lord, then what wise person would have undertaken the trouble of these webs of speech? (BhStc 40)
O Lord, by what gradual process, by what action, or by what wisdom may You become visible? Please grant me grace through Your instruction.
Homage to the one who has no need for assistance, the sole benefactor of the three worlds,
the object of desire for all, yet himself free from longing— the one with matted hair.
Oh, how great is this field-knowledge of the virtuous for the sake of their purpose, by which they sow devotion unto you, O Lord, which yields infinite fruit! (BhStc 43)
Oh, how great is this illusion of yours, O Master of Illusion! Enveloped by it, the world remains bewildered and slackens even when attaining the treasure-trove of meditation upon you.
Let there be action everywhere at the beginning, whether it be the act itself or the instrument and so forth;
let the universe be so, but you alone shall be its independent creator therein.
Who else besides you has the power or the compassion to uplift the three worlds, which are seized by the three qualities, the threefold fluctuations, and the pairs of opposites?
What fault indeed could there be for one who has set out to attain you? And what merit indeed could there not be for one who has set out to attain you?
O Lord of the World, let there be passion for you alone, which resides within me;
even to that greed I offer salutation, for it takes as its object the attainment of you.
Oh, how great is this deed of yours, O Lord, which consists of your own meditative cultivation!
Within it, who among us—from Brahmā down to a mere worm—is not qualified for liberation?
The commencement of all undertakings and the conclusion of all actions— the various activities occurring between them— belong to you alone, O Lord, on the path of the intellect.
O Lord, the nectar of the flavor of devotion to you is not seen anywhere else; its excellence increases a thousandfold with every subsequent taste.
Homage to the Lord Soma, who has withdrawn all desires, who does not extend the prospect of desire, and who has the moon as his crest-ornament.
For me, who am unable to act and thus find no resolution in any direction, thinking "What shall I do?", may the all-beneficent power of Śaṅkara be my refuge.
O Lord, where among the various states of existence can a supreme substitute be found for you, who have transcended all qualities and whose nature consists of every excellence without exception?
O Lord, while you— the Self, free from duality and beyond all limiting conditions— exist,
we are still deceived today by your unfathomable *māyā*.
The attainment of qualities such as atomization (aṇimā), eternal sovereignty, and the destruction of worldly existence—
these, O Lord, are the sprouts of the wish-fulfilling tree that is devotion to you.
"In whichever direction one looks, you are not there; yet all time is composed of you.
O Lord, tell me: though you have been found, when will you be truly attained? BhStc_56
Homage to Śambhu, the Great Swan, whose body is whitened by abundant ashes and who is the sole abode for the minds of those with pure and virtuous conduct.
O Lord, may the lamp of your awakening be my lamp of devotion— a lamp that has uprooted the darkness of delusion and its exhaustion, and which has consumed all the fuel of cyclic existence.
O Hara, who else but you is capable of being the poet to compose and then dissolve this drama of the three worlds, which contains within its womb many excellent seeds that have been sown?

Homage to the one who alone possesses sovereign power over both the existent and the non-existent, who is both independent and dependent, and who acts to bring about either the non-existence or the very existence of things.
I pay homage to that god, the ocean of bliss, of whom whatever joy is seen here in the three worlds constitutes but a single drop.
Oh, how blessed are Brahmā and the others, who, free from idle chatter, are overwhelmed with joy as they mutter: "Obeisance, obeisance to Śiva! (BhStc 62)
Salutations be to You, O Bhava, who bestows infinite desires even upon those free from desire, and who is the enjoyer of the universe despite its beginninglessness.
We praise the Lord, the primordial nature at the beginning of the three worlds;
for who would fail to receive benefit from Him, whose nature is perfectly complete?
We praise that Śiva, by whose remembrance minds become serene even amidst great hardships, having been purified from the turbid flood of delusion.
O Lord, yours alone is this unyielding power of lordship here,
by whose will the dissolution and arising of the three worlds are extended.
Even an evil deed becomes a supreme good deed when performed for the sake of that deity; since there is no such excellence in goodness found elsewhere, O Lord, you are indeed he.
"You are caught by my fist! Now that you have been seen, where can you go from us?
Thus, the blessed ones, swelling with the sentiment of devotion, run after Dhūrjaṭi.
We praise you, who are beyond the Śukra and further than the supreme, through the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāman Vedas;
whose command, consisting of the Vedas, is unknowable—oh, how profound and beautiful!
O Supreme Lord, you are the beginning, the end, and likewise the source of the universe;
how could that multitude of dharmas which has proceeded from you not exist?
Homage to you, O God, who, having manifested and then shattered the delusion of those bewildered by existence,
disclose the non-dual bliss of primordial wisdom after having embraced it.
May Śiva protect us— he who, in a single blink of an eye, steals away that illusion whose specific limits cannot be reached by any desires.
O Lord, you are the sovereign of those who bear the profound course of dispassion, the supreme glory of knowledge, and the ultimate pinnacle of desirelessness.
You are the Brahman even of Brahmā; who does not acknowledge you as the Lord of the Lord?
Who can know how great you are, you who are the auspiciousness of the world's welfare?
What need have I for other kinsmen, friends, or masters?
For in every circumstance, O Lord, you are my savior from the ocean of existence.
Victorious are the divine droplets of nectar, drawn forth by the power of Śaiva yoga, which are capable of washing away the impurities of delusion, illusion, and the like.
May that Lord, whose splendor is chanted by the Gāyatrī and who impels the brilliance of our intellects, also inspire our thoughts toward the path of truth.
O Eight-formed One, why do you not grant us eternal stability even in a single form? Or rather, if you are pleased, you will surely accomplish everything.
The true nature of things generally consists in their capacity for causal efficiency;
yet for you, O Lord, even your name alone bestows the attainment of liberation as its ultimate fruit.
O Lord, what wise person would not be struck with wonder by that power of yours which, moment after moment, conceives of ever-new states for the wondrous painting of the world?
We remember that enemy of Māra, for whom mindfulness— the sole hero— is able to make the difficult easy and likewise transform suffering into happiness.
Victorious are those songs whose subject is that Supreme Lord,
by whose very name great souls are covered with sprouts of horripilation.
O Bhava, if you alone were to become like yourself—
possessing the creation and destruction of the three worlds through the array of your own manifold powers— then that would be supreme.
You are the mantra, you are the one to be addressed with mantras, and you are the counselor; from whom else could [such a thing] come?
O Lord, grant that mantra to me, so that I may become one whose mantra is yours.
I too am that very Self of yours, who is of the nature of light and whose volitions are true;
how then can this transmigrating being be the Lord? This must be a dream, and even that dream—how could it exist within you?
O Lord, that sovereignty which belongs to those who have surrendered the fruits of their actions unto You is unbroken, refined, singular, and endowed with reason.
What misfortune is he unable to destroy, or what prosperity is he unable to bestow?
He who is thus is our beloved, the God of gods, whose banner bears the bull.
O Lord, devotion to you is the supreme collyrium for purifying the divine eye of wisdom, which is blinded by the impurity of illusion.
"O God, grant me that state which is fearless, which consists of bliss, which is one and imperishable; come to me quickly, why do you wait? (BhStc 89)
Oh, how profound and terrible by nature is this ocean of saṃsāra!
Oh, how extraordinary is Maheśvara, the supreme means for crossing it!
Homage to you, who have brought an end to Death himself, the crusher of Madana,
who bears the Gaṅgā upon his head, and who accomplishes the purpose as it truly is.
O Protector, for those who seek a state even higher than sovereignty, knowledge, dispassion, and virtue,
what other refuge is there but you?
O Śambhu, if you do not will it, who is able to bend even a blade of grass?
But who, favored by your will, would not bear the burden of Brahmā?
Whom else would those rich in wisdom bow to, whose heads are crowned with the crest-jewels of prostration before the Lord; or whom could they possibly cause to bow down? (BhStc 94)
O Dhūrjaṭi, may I dwell even within the midst of the ocean of your wisdom— a lake of nectar, unshakable and free from all delusion.
It is marvelous, O Protector, that even when seen in a painting, or even when existing only as an object of the mind's desire,
you bestow the full fruit of the ultimate truth.
"Who is superior to you in virtues? Who is more devoid of virtues than you?
O Lord, we do not know whether to praise you or to revile you. Thus we do not understand what to do.
O Lord of the World, who else is capable even of drinking that fruit which results from Your grace when there is the chanting of the flood of nectar? How much less so of bestowing it?
O Lord, since you are the treasury that accomplishes the entire multitude of all things to be desired without exception,
I pray to you in every way only to obtain devotion to you.
Homage to you, the Lord of the three worlds,
who possesses the power to remove obstacles for those dwelling in existence by bestowing lordship over the three worlds.
When doubt arises as to what is the cause for the total abandonment of all afflictions, who would not go to you for refuge, having resolved with certainty: "O Lord, you are that very cause"?

"Having enjoyed worldly pleasures and abandoned the wandering through existence, I shall attain the supreme state"—such a hope here would be fitting for one who possesses supreme devotion to Śambhu. (BhStc 102)
O Lord, whatever I might do or say, whether good or bad— even in a dream—
I am everywhere at ease here, through the pride of being dependent upon you.
O Lord, for one who runs toward Your abode— the light even of lights—
I consider the touch of darkness in the mind to be like the younger brother of the son of a barren woman.
I believe that even his desire—"May I serve Śiva"—is one who has already set foot upon the secure path to liberation. (BhStc 105)
In this world, regarding the benefits for the three realms through maintenance, arising, and dissolution,
O Lord, you perceive Your own independent power as the sole autonomous tantra.
In these three worlds, who has been protected, and who has not been tormented by the triple affliction? Homage be to you, who are that lake of the nectar of nirvāṇa!
"Even artificial devotion to you results in genuine fruit; if this [devotion] were free from deceit, tell me, what kind of fruit could it not produce? (BhStc 108)
O Unborn One, that eye by which You are beheld and that path by which You are reached has become its fruit, arising from the wish-fulfilling tree that is Your story.
This very state of yours, which abides above all that is auspicious, is itself the highest good; O Lord, you are my refuge for the removal of obstacles to that [good].
Oh, how most delicious is this nectar-like essence of the aspiration for service to Śarva,
which does not grow old even in the mere fraction of a moment!

Victorious is that certain unborn One, who, though incessantly conceptualizing the three worlds through hundreds of mental constructions moment after moment, remains himself free from conceptual construction.
O Lord, when shall I stand before you with the lamp of knowledge, which burns away the wick of worldly tendencies soaked in the oil of impurity?
O Śambhu, if you were to place even a single step upon the mind for a mere moment once its defects have been exhausted, then what would you not accomplish?
O Lord, for one who takes you as his object, the thought "I am blessed," "I have accomplished my purpose," and "I am great" would have you as its objective support.
O Lord, you yourself are the creator of all that is auspicious and inauspicious;
yet your devotion is the mother of auspiciousness alone.
"O Lord, when the mind is already serene, why do you enter it? Or rather, does it become serene because of your entry?"—thus the people waver in doubt. (BhStc 117)
Furthermore, the certainty in this matter is simply your own empowerment; O Lord, it is the clarity of the mind, that is accomplishment, that is the supreme state.
O Lord, by your grace, may my speech, mind, actions, and body become solely adorned with the state of being [absorbed] in you.
Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa has composed this *Stavacintāmaṇi*, which bestows the fruit of abundant desires, and which is the abode of the fortune of devotion to Śambhu. (BhStc 120)
